SDF-guided Sampling is a surface-aware sampling strategy that uses a Signed Distance Field (SDF) to estimate ray-surface intersections, followed by fine-grained sampling around the intersection point to accelerate rendering and emphasize the relationship between surface and radiance fields [S1, S2].

The claim states that SDF-guided Sampling is a surface-aware strategy using SDF to estimate intersections, followed by fine-grained sampling to accelerate rendering and emphasize the surface-radiance relationship. Source [S1] explicitly mentions that Shao et al. use the SDF field to guide surface sampling by estimating ray-surface intersections and performing fine-grained sampling around the intersection point. Source [S2] describes a 'Surface-guided Sampling Strategy' that determines intersection points in the surface field first, then performs fine-grained sampling around the intersected surface to accelerate the rendering process and emphasize the relation between the two fields. Both sources corroborate the specific mechanisms (SDF/surface field usage, intersection estimation, fine-grained sampling) and the stated benefits (acceleration, emphasizing relationship) mentioned in the claim.
